Independence and space: new homes a step forward after family violence

Women with older children were not getting support, service says.

Actual Article Body:

When Carly was 25 weeks pregnant with her twins, she was couch surfing with friends, or living in a motel.

Login or signup to continue reading

Carly, whose name has been changed, had left the father of her children because of domestic violence but was not eligible for public housing because she had only lived in the ACT for eight weeks.

Her older children, then 5 and 7 years old, could not be enrolled in school because she had no fixed address. She worried the stress would affect her pregnancy.

Eventually, Carly was offered a place at one of the transitional cottages at Karinya House, a support service for women who are pregnant or who have recently given birth.

Karinya House was able to support Carly through the birth of her twins and the post-partum period, but it soon became clear the two-bedroom house was not suitable for a family of five.

The twins began crawling, and the older children could not have their friends over because the location is kept confidential to protect the residents.

Karinya House chief executive Lavinia Tyrrel said there was a cohort of young mothers the support service could not support in their current accommodation.

"If you have older children, it becomes more challenging to keep the security arrangements in place," Ms Tyrrel said.

"We've also got shared living for part of it, so having toddlers and multiple children in a shared living space is really challenging."

Carly was one of 41 women who were assessed by Karinya House between 2023 and 2025 who Ms Tyrrel said might have been served by a different type of transitional housing, which would have fewer security restrictions and larger living spaces.

Through a partnership with Karinya House, community housing provider Community Housing Canberra is now building three houses it hopes will bridge this gap.

The houses will provide a "step down" from the 24-7 wraparound care women and children living at Karinya House's current accommodation receive, allowing for more independence and space.

Ms Tyrrel said crisis housing for women continued to be in high demand because of domestic violence, the housing crisis and the worsening cost of living.
